title: Generic localization and completion cover for the reduced projectivity induction
statement: Let $R$ be a nonzero reduced Noetherian commutative ring (reduced means no nonzero nilpotent elements), and let $R\to S$ be a finite type flat homomorphism of commutative rings. Suppose that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $S\otimes_R K$ is a nonzero integral domain, and that $S/JS$ is projective over $R/J$ for every nonzero ideal $J\subseteq R$. Then there exists $0\ne f\in R$ such that $S_f=S\otimes_R R_f$ is a free $R_f$-module (a direct sum of copies of $R_f$, with arbitrary index set). For this same $f$, put $A=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/(f^n)$ and $N=S\otimes_R A$. The canonical map $R\to R_f\times A$ is faithfully flat, $A$ is Noetherian and $fA$-adically complete, and the projection induces an $R$-algebra isomorphism $A/fA\cong R/(f)$. The map $A\to N$ is finite type and flat, and $N\otimes_A L$ is a nonzero integral domain for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Finally the canonical map induces $N/fN\cong S/fS$ over $A/fA\cong R/(f)$, and $N/fN$ is projective over $A/fA$. The notions are [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], [def-weil-ring-localization-away], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Fix this same $f$, and put $A=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/(f^n)$. The hypotheses of [lem-trf-local-completion-product-faithfully-flat] hold: $R$ is reduced Noetherian and $f\ne0$. Hence $R\to R_f\times A$ is faithfully flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $A$ is Noetherian. The ideal $(f)$ is generated by one element, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] gives $fA$-adic completeness and the projection-induced $R$-algebra isomorphism $A/fA\cong R/(f)$, whose composite with $R\to A$ is reduction modulo $f$.

proof.text: Put $N=S\otimes_R A$ with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(s'\otimes a')=ss'\otimes aa'$. The elements $s_i\otimes1$ generate $N$ as an $A$-algebra: write each $s$ as a polynomial in the $s_i$, and then each $s\otimes a$ as that polynomial in $s_i\otimes1$ with its coefficients multiplied by $a$; pure tensors generate the tensor product additively. This proves finite type directly from [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] to the flat $R$-module $S$ and $R\to A$; it gives flatness of $A\otimes_R S$. The flip $a\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes a$, inverse to the same flip, is $A$-linear by the tensor relations. Hence $N$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tags 00F3 (definition-finite-type), 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) and 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change); base-change assertion in flat.tex Tag 05FS

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be prime, set $\mathfrak p=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset R$, and let $L/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ be a field extension. The map $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is injective and sends every nonzero element to a unit, so the fraction formula $\bar r/\bar u\mapsto\iota(r)/\iota(u)$ extends it to an embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. In particular $L$ is a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The tensor relations give inverse $L$-algebra maps $(S\otimes_R A)\otimes_A L\leftrightarrows S\otimes_R L$, namely $(s\otimes a)\otimes l\mapsto s\otimes al$ and $s\otimes l\mapsto(s\otimes1)\otimes l$. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. The latter algebra is a nonzero domain by the original fibre hypothesis, proving the required assertion for $N\otimes_A L$.

proof.text: Use the isomorphism of Step 3 to regard $\bar a\in A/fA$ as an element of $R/(f)$. Define $N\to S/fS$ on pure tensors by $s\otimes a\mapsto\bar s\,\bar a$. Balancing follows because $R\to A/fA\cong R/(f)$ is the quotient map. This homomorphism kills $fN$, and so induces $\theta:N/fN\to S/fS$. In the other direction $s\mapsto[s\otimes1]$ kills $fS$, defining $\eta:S/fS\to N/fN$. Clearly $\theta\eta=1$. For the other composite, choose $r\in R$ representing $\bar a\in R/(f)$; then $a-\iota(r)\in fA$, and $[s\otimes a]=[s\otimes\iota(r)]=[rs\otimes1]$. Thus $\eta\theta=1$ on the additive pure-tensor generators. Both maps respect the scalar identification $A/fA\cong R/(f)$, proving the claimed canonical algebra isomorphism.

source.place: flat.tex Tag 05FS, equality S/fS=(S tensor_R R-hat)/f(S tensor_R R-hat); expanded using Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Since $f\ne0$, the ideal $J=(f)$ is nonzero, and the hypothesis with this $J$ says that $S/fS$ is projective over $R/(f)$. The compatible ring and module isomorphisms in Steps 3 and 6 carry a splitting of a free module onto $S/fS$ to a splitting of the corresponding free $A/fA$-module onto $N/fN$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Hence $N/fN$ is projective. This includes $f$ a unit: then $A=0$, both quotient rings and quotient modules are zero, and the same splitting is valid.
